subject: Discovery recap: FinTechCorp Private VPC & on-prem requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@fintechcorp.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: FinTechCorp Private VPC & on-prem requirements

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time today — I appreciate the walkthrough of your current architecture and requirements. Below is a short recap of what we heard, success criteria, open questions, and proposed next steps. Please reply with any corrections.

Summary of pain points and goals
- Regulated workloads require all inference traffic and model serving to run inside a customer-managed VPC (no egress to public internet).
- Must support on-prem or air-gapped deployment option for PII/regulated flows in Q4.
- Customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) required for model artifacts and request-level logging; ability to rotate keys on schedule.
- Network constraints: strict outbound rules, limited NAT, and strict IP allowlist for all control-plane callbacks.
- Need audit-ready logs (S3-compatible retention) and SOC2 evidence for security reviews.

Current stack (what you shared)
- Core services: Kubernetes on AWS (EKS) for internal services; several legacy batches on bare-metal in co-lo for highest-sensitivity workloads.
- Identity: Okta with SCIM; central KMS is AWS KMS with HSM-backed keys for some data.
- Networking: Transit gateway with strict egress rules; only certain CIDR ranges allowed.

Success criteria (MVP for pilot)
- Private deployment in customer VPC with no public egress from inference nodes.
- Support for customer-managed KMS with ability to use HSM and rotate keys without service downtime.
- Verified audit logs + retention policy (90 days) and access controls for security team.
- End-to-end latency for 2kQPS baseline (internal benchmark) within 30% of hosted latency.

Open questions / clarifications
1) For the on-prem/air-gap scenario: can you confirm the preferred timeline and which workloads must be air-gapped vs. allowed in VPC?
2) Do we need integration with your HSM vendor (Thales)? Or will AWS KMS with imported key material suffice for pilot?
3) For control-plane callbacks (metrics/alerts), do you have a jump-host or outbound proxy we should plan for, or do we need to support a polling-only control plane?

Attachments
- redwood-private-vpc-checklist.pdf (initial checklist we discussed)
- FT-2026-045-mutual-action-plan.xlsx (outline of milestones / responsibilities)

Proposed next steps
- I will loop in our solutions engineering lead (Jonas) to schedule a technical deep-dive next week focused on networking and KMS integration.
- You (Alex/Priya) to confirm air-gap timeline and whether Thales HSM integration is required.
- Exchange NDA / compliance intake docs (we can send SOC2 artifact links after initial NDA).

If that looks right, I'll coordinate Jonas to set up the technical session and include our security engineer for the compliance questions.

Thanks,

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com | (415) 555-0192
https://redwood.inference.com
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@fintechcorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@fintechcorp.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 08:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: FinTechCorp Private VPC & on-prem requirements

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the summary — that aligns well. A few clarifications below: 

- Air-gap timeline: we're targeting a pilot in the VPC for Q2 (May) and planning the air-gapped on-prem work for our Q4 compliance window (approx Oct). For the pilot, only the non-PII flows will be in the VPC; the PII-sensitive flows must stay in on-prem or air-gapped nodes.
- HSM: For Q2 pilot, AWS KMS with imported key material should be fine. For Q4 (air-gap), we will need Thales HSM integration for the highest-sensitivity paths.
- Control-plane: We do not have a persistent outbound proxy; security prefers a polling model for control-plane interactions during air-gapped mode. For VPC pilot, we can allow outbound to a limited set of IPs via NAT.

A couple of asks from our side: 
1) Can you confirm that Redwood's private control plane supports polling-only mode (no callbacks) for air-gapped nodes?
2) Can you provide a short checklist of networking/IP ranges your infra will need to be allowed for the VPC pilot?

CC'ing Priya to validate the compliance timeline.

Best,
Alex

On Mon, Feb 16, 2026 at 08:10 AM Priya Rao <priya.rao@fintechcorp.com> wrote:
> +1 on the timeline. Also, can we get the SOC2 artifact link once NDA is in place?
> 
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: FinTechCorp Private VPC & on-prem requirements

Thanks Alex — that is really helpful. Quick replies inline: 

- Polling-only control plane: yes — we have a polling mode for air-gapped deployments. Jonas (cc'd) will cover the technical details in the deep-dive.
- Networking/IP ranges: attaching the initial IP range list and the checklist. For the VPC pilot we only need to allow a small set of egress IPs; I've attached FT-2026-045-mutual-action-plan.xlsx with the draft ranges.
- SOC2 artifacts: we'll share SOC2 evidence over the secure link once the NDA is signed.

Next steps (owned):
- Marissa: send NDA template and SOC2 intake link (by EOD 2/16) — DONE (link + attachment).
- Jonas: schedule technical deep-dive (networking & KMS) for week of 2/23.
- FinTechCorp (Alex/Priya): confirm air-gap timeline (Q4) and Thales need for on-prem.

Jonas — can you propose 2 times for the deep-dive? I'll coordinate calendars.

Thanks,

--
